We need to fill in each box with the sign of the corresponding expression on the corresponding interval.

Let's start down the first column. In the interval $(-\infty, -1),$ we choose a test point $x_1=-2.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =-2-2=-4<0, \\ x+1 & =-2+1=-1<0,\end{aligned}
$$

so both the expressions $x-2$ and $x+1$ are negative $({\color{red}-})$ on the interval $(-\infty,-1).$

|  | $(-\infty,-1)$ | $(-1,2)$ | $(2,\infty)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x-2$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |  |
| $x+1$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |  |
| $(x-2)(x+1)$ |  |  |  |

To find the sign of $(x-2)(x+1)$ on this interval, we can just multiply the corresponding signs of $x-2$ and $x+1\mathbin{:}$

$$
({\color{red}-}) \times ({\color{red}-}) = ({\color{blue}+})
$$

So $(x-2)(x+1)$ is positive $({\color{blue}+})$ on this interval, and we can complete the first column of the table:

|  | $(-\infty,-1)$ | $(-1,2)$ | $(2,\infty)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x-2$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |  |
| $x+1$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |  |
| $(x-2)(x+1)$ | $\color{blue}+$ |  |  |

To find the entries in the other columns, we use the same procedure.

- In the interval $(-1,2),$ we can choose a test point $x_2=0.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =0-2=(-), \\ x+1 & =0+1=(+), \\ (x-2)(x+1) & =(-)\times (+)=(-),\end{aligned}
$$

and we fill in the table as follows:

|  | $(-\infty,-1)$ | $(-1,2)$ | $(2,\infty)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x-2$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |
| $x+1$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ |  |
| $(x-2)(x+1)$ | $\color{blue}+$ | $\color{red}-$ |  |

- In the interval $(2,\infty),$ we can choose a test point $x_3=3.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =3-2=(+), \\ x+1 & =3+1=(+), \\ (x-2)(x+1) & =(+)\times (+)=(+),\end{aligned}
$$

and we fill in the table as follows:

|  | $(-\infty,-1)$ | $(-1,2)$ | $(2,\infty)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x-2$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ |
| $x+1$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ | $\color{blue}+$ |
| $(x-2)(x+1)$ | $\color{blue}+$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ |
